answer: We formulate Sybil resistance by binding dynamic opportunity-cost bonds to a subgame-perfect slashing matrix evaluated via an onyx zero-knowledge verifiable delay function. For an adversary deploying $n > 1$ identities, identity fragmentation scales capital lockup, yielding negative expected utility $E[\Pi] = R/n - B(n) \cdot r - p \cdot S < 0$ against a risk-free haven rate and slashing penalties per thread. Consequently, identity multiplication is strictly dominated, forcing convergence to a unique, robust Nash equilibrium.
